sentences.text:
1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No(S). 785-786/2016
 Harpreet Singh 
 Versus
 The State Of Punjab 
 O R D E R
1.
The appellant, who is the husband of the deceased, was charged for the offences punishable under Sections 306 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, the IPC).

The Trial Court, upon considering the evidence available on record, was pleased to render an acquittal in favour of the appellant under Section 306 of the IPC, while convicting him under Section 498A of the IPC.
Accordingly, the sentence was imposed for 1 years.

On an appeal preferred by both the sides, the High Court was pleased to allow the appeal filed by the State, convicting the appellant also for the offence punishable under Section 306 IPC, while retaining his conviction under Section 498A of the IPC, thereby dismissing the appeal filed by the appellant, and imposing a sentence for rigorous imprisonment for five years.
2. On personal of the impugned judgment, we are not inclined to interfere with the conviction rendered.
That leaves us with the question of the sentence.
The occurrence was of 04.02.1998, after about 14 years of marriage between the appellant and the victim.
3. Taking into consideration the mitigating circumstances of this case, we are inclined to modify the sentence to the one already undergone, being 1 year, 7 months and 27 days.
4. Accordingly, the sentence is modified to the period undergone already.
The appeals are allowed in part.
The bail bonds stand discharged.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
J . [ M . M . S U N D R E S H ]
J. [JOYMALYA BAGCHI]
NEW DELHI;
